L26·N9817unmasked layer
This neuron fires almost exclusively at sentence/clause boundaries — the terminal period or newline ending a declarative statement (with a few final-word-of-phrase peaks) — and it is the same punctuation position that drives its extreme negative values, so it looks like a sentence-end marker detector rather than a semantic feature.

L31·N4989unmasked layer
This neuron has no clean semantic content — it fires on "glue" tokens inside highly predictable multi-token continuations (list commas, " or"/" to" in fixed phrases, whitespace inside a duration, subword pieces of long names like "Sah|ar|awis" / "S|clerosis"), and is strongly suppressed by the indefinite article " a".

L31·N8648unmasked layer
Rather than a semantic category, this neuron tracks register/position: it peaks on mid-phrase continuation tokens (function words like " I", " in", " and", " an", or a word-piece such as the "a" of "Tabitha") inside casual, concrete narrative prose, while it is strongly *suppressed* by abstract head nouns that close a formal expository noun phrase right before a period (e.g. "aspects.", "role.", "technologies", "assets.").
